item.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
item.description: An artist’s concept depicting a Voyager spacecraft. Credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight this historic milestone with two events. On Tuesday, Nov. 17, NASA invites the world to participate in “Shine Bright for Voyager’s Light-Day” by creating a symbolic wave of golden light encircling the planet after sunset. NASA has created a website that enables smart phones and tablets to flash “VGR”, Voyager’s call sign, in morse code. For more information about how to participate in “Shine Bright for Voyager Light-Day,” visit: go.nasa.gov/shinebright Everyone is encouraged to capture photos or videos of their light-day signal and share it on social platforms, tagging @NASA. On Thursday, Nov. 19 at 12 p.m. EST (9 a.m. PST), NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California will host a moderated discussion with mission members and NASA leadership about the status of Voyager 1 and 2, the unique science the twin probes continue to gather in interstellar space, and the challenges of keeping the spacecraft operating for so long over such vast distances. A Q&A with media and other audience members will follow. In addition, there also will be a preview of the upcoming NASA+ Voyager documentary, planned for release in 2027 for the mission’s 50th anniversary. The event will take place in NASA JPL’s von Kármán Auditorium, where JPL hosted Voyager briefings during the spacecraft’s grand tour of the outer planets. The participants will be: Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, Washington Jonathan Lunine, chief scientist, NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Southern California, and professor of planetary science, Caltech Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager, NASA JPL Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager, NASA JPL Jamie Rankin, Voyager deputy project scientist, Princeton University Learn where to watch online at: https://www.nasa.gov/live U.S. media interested in attending the event in person must RSVP by Monday, Nov. 16 to Josh Smooha at: josh.smooha@jpl.nasa.gov . To be considered for onsite credentials, foreign national media must RSVP no later than Thursday, Nov. 12. Media interested in participating virtually must RSVP no later than two hours before the event. NASA’s media accreditation policy is available online. For almost half a century, the agency’s Voyager mission has blazed a trail through space. Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 were designed to explore the outer planets by taking advantage of a planetary alignment that occurs once every 176 years. Voyager 1 entered interstellar space in 2012. Following a different trajectory, Voyager 2 entered in 2018. Both spacecraft continue to provide unique scientific observations o

item.title: Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review Poland’s lower house of parliament voted 240-202 on Friday to let the interior minister freeze crypto assets, bank accounts and other property of people placed on a national sanctions list, before any court reviews the order. The Sejm, Poland’s lower house, passed the Act on Restrictive Measures at its 68th sitting, with one member abstaining and 17 not voting. The Senate received the bill Monday and has 30 days under Article 121 of the Constitution to adopt, amend or reject it, after which it would go to President Karol Nawrocki. The law, a government bill that also implements European Union sanctions rules, treats crypto assets as financial means that can be frozen, using the definition in the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. A freeze, as the text defines it, is meant to stop any movement, transfer, use or other change that would let the holder benefit from the assets. The freeze applies only to people and entities the interior minister adds to a public national list, either on the minister’s own initiative or at the request of agencies that include the financial watchdog, the central bank, the financial intelligence unit and the internal security service. Grounds include supporting a country already under EU sanctions, serious human rights abuses, or initiating or financing information manipulation that poses a serious threat to Poland’s national security. A listing on that last ground requires a showing of a real and serious threat to Poland’s interests, borders, security or elections. The bill carves out ordinary journalism, political speech and publishing, unless that activity is a knowing campaign of the kind the law describes. A freeze that starts before a judge weighs in The interior minister’s decision takes effect the day after it is posted in the ministry’s Public Information Bulletin and is immediately enforceable. There is no request to the minister to reconsider. A listed person may file a complaint with an administrative court, but the law says the decision remains in force until a judgment becomes final, and it sets aside the usual rule that would let a court pause a challenged order. The measures also bar making funds or property available to listed persons and can exclude them from public contracts. In some cases, the economy minister may appoint a temporary administrator to sell frozen assets or, under a separate order, take them over for the State Treasury. What the freeze would mean for bitcoin The Poland bill does not target ordinary bitcoin holders in Poland. It reaches crypto assets owned, held or under the control of people and firms on the sanctions list. Banks, exchanges and other parties face administrative fines if they fail to freeze those assets or make them available, and compliance is checked by the financial intelligence unit and the Polish Financial Supervision Authority for the firms they already over

item.title: Nobody Said The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Was This Funny
item.description: Though I’ve never played The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time until now, I’ve heard people sing its praises for years. Mostly, this revolved around its impossibly high score of 99 on Metacritic, its influential open world and combat design, and its memorable dungeons. But none of those ardent fans bothered to tell me that this classic game has some genuinely hilarious moments. Because the game was originally released 28 years ago, a spoiler-free experience is pretty much off the table for me. But the goofs and gags? Those are all 100% fresh.

item.title: Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – No fewer than three persons have reportedly been killed following an attack by gunmen on a mining site in Jol community, Riyom Local Government Area of Plateau State. The incident occurred at about 6pm on Tuesday, when the assailants reportedly stormed the mining site and opened fire on people in the area. A resident of the community, Bulus Shen, who confirmed the incident, told newsmen that the gunmen arrived at the mining site in the evening and began shooting sporadically. Shen said the attack threw the community into panic, adding that three persons were reportedly killed in the incident. The spokesperson of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), Rwang Tengwong, also confirmed the attack. Tengwong condemned the killing, describing the incident as disturbing and unacceptable. He called on security agencies to urgently investigate the attack, apprehend those responsible and strengthen security around rural communities to prevent further loss of lives. Efforts to get further details from security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Three feared killed as gunmen attack mining site in Plateau appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Abia 2027: Agbazuere makes U-turn, backs Otti’s 2nd term bid
item.description: . Dismisses Ogbonnaya’s alleged anti-Ngwa claim, warns critics By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who strongly opposed Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has thrown his weight behind the governor’s re-election bid, declaring that he deserves a second term. Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed allegations credited to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated. Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere warned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, saying defamatory statements could attract civil and criminal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act. He said the allegation posed no threat to Otti’s political support base, particularly among the Ngwa people. “Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. Anybody who wants to say anything should be careful and say what he knows to be true,” he warned. Explaining his support for the governor, Agbazuere said Otti’s administration had demonstrated commitment to infrastructure development, urban renewal, workers’ welfare and good governance. He cited the reconstruction of Port Harcourt Road and Bank Road in Aba, the Omenuko Bridge and Arochukwu Road as evidence of the administration’s infrastructure drive. He also commended the governor for regular payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities, as well as improvements in traditional rulers’ allowances. On criticisms that increased federal allocations should have translated into more projects, Agbazuere argued that the rising cost of construction materials must be considered, citing the increase in cement prices from about N2,000 to N12,000 per bag. He challenged critics to visit the state and assess ongoing projects rather than judge the administration from a distance. Describing Otti as a banker and trained economist, he said the governor understood accountability and prudent management of public resources. Agbazuere urged Abians to look beyond party affiliations and support continuity, arguing that a second term would enable Otti to complete ongoing projects and consolidate his administration’s programmes. He recalled that even during the 2023 election, a leading opposition governorship candidate had reportedly acknowledged Otti as the best candidate. Vanguard reports that Agbazuere, a former Commissioner for Information, was among Otti’s vocal critics but recently switched allegiance after dumping the All Progressives Congress (APC), where he briefly sought political shelter shortly after Otti assumed office in 2023. He hails from the same Isiala Ngwa South Local Government Area with Gov. Otti. The post Abia 2027: Agbazuere makes U-turn, ba

item.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
item.description: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. If we compare these planets to Earth , which has a stable magnetic field tilted by just 11 degrees to our planet’s rotation, we can see how extreme the magnetic fields of the ice giants are. Various explanations for the strange magnetic fields of the ice giants have been put forward over the years. Uranus as a whole is tilted by 97 degrees and effectively rolls around the sun , and speculation is that billions of years ago it was knocked on its side by a collision with a long-lost Earth-sized planet. Could this collision have also skewed its magnetic field? This might be a plausible explanation were Neptune’s magnetic field also not similarly skewed without having experienced a collision. Clearly, whatever the cause, it must be intrinsic to the nature of the two ice giant planets. Now, a new study by scientists in the U.S. and the UK, based on computer simulations and Voyager 2’s measurements of the two planets’ magnetic fields, may have found a solution. The solution to the weird magnetic fields of the solar system's ice giants may come down to how planets generate their magnetic field through the dynamo effect. This arises from the swirling, convective motion of an electrically conducting liquid within a rotating body, which is able to generate and maintain a powerful magnetic field. Inside Earth, the electrically conducting fluid is the molten iron in the outer part of our planet’s core, and the magnetic field that it generates has clear north and south poles – what we call a dipole, a phenomenon that we can also see in the two magnetic poles of a simple bar magnet. However, the conditions inside Uranus and Neptune are somewhat different. As ice giants, they contain a lot of volatiles – ammonia, hydrogen, helium, methane, and water surrounding a probable rocky core. Furthermore, Uranus and Neptune are substantially larger than Earth , with 14.5 and 17 times the mass of our planet, respectively. This increased mass creates crushing conditions within the interior of the ice giants. "Deep inside Uranus and Neptune, pressures and temperatures become extremely high," research team leader Chi Yan of the University of Texas at Austin, who led the new find

item.title: 2027: Avoid technicalities, treat electronic evidence rigorously, INEC charges tribunals
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has urged members of the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals to avoid technicalities that defeat substantive justice and to subject electronic evidence to rigorous scrutiny. He also told them to keep firm control of their courtrooms and let “truth of the ballot prevail”. According to the commission’s Daily Bulletin of Tuesday, Amupitan spoke on Monday in Abuja while delivering the Commission’s opening remarks at a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the tribunals, held at the Body of Benchers Complex. The Court of Appeal organised the workshop under the theme “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability.” The INEC chairman said electoral litigation had grown more complex, with disputes now touching on voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results, technological failures and the integrity of digital records. On the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), he said technology should neither be treated as infallible nor dismissed simply because the evidence is electronic. Amupitan warned that digital disinformation driven by artificial intelligence, audio cloning and deepfake videos would inevitably spill into the courtrooms. He urged the tribunals to apply strict evidentiary standards under Section 84 of the Evidence Act, saying digital provenance, forensic chain of custody and reliance on certified data from INEC would be vital to stop synthetic fabrications from misleading the courts. He added that electoral adjudication is evidence-driven, and that allegations of irregularities, non-compliance or result manipulation must be proved with credible and legally admissible evidence. According to him, the Commission has issued the Regulations and Guidelines for the Conduct of Elections, 2026, to give clearer operational standards against which claims of non-compliance can be weighed in proceedings. The INEC chairman told the tribunal members that they carry the democratic aspirations of over 200 million Nigerians once they take their oaths. He described the courtroom as the altar on which public confidence in constitutional governance is preserved, and urged them to let their decisions reflect deep fidelity to the law, uncompromising integrity and the principle that justice must be seen to be done. Amupitan said Nigeria’s political stability in 2027 would depend not only on how efficiently INEC conducts elections, but also on how courageously, transparently and justly the tribunals settle the disputes that follow. He described the Election Petition Tribunal as a constitutional valve that releases political pressure and keeps electoral friction from degenerating into civil disruption. A tribunal that acts with procedural speed, evidentiary rigour and absolute impartiality, he said, assures aggrieved parties that a credible platform exists to assess t

item.title: Makinde presents N1.12trn final budget
item.description: …Allocates 60% to capital expenditure …Dismisses appointees’ resignations as meaningless By Adeola Badru Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Tuesday presented a proposed N1.12 trillion budget for the 2027 fiscal year to the State House of Assembly, describing it as the “Budget of Sustained Progress”, while dismissing the recent resignations of political appointees as inconsequential. Makinde said the departure of some officials from his administration would not distract his government or affect its commitment to delivering its mandate. The governor made the remarks while presenting the 2027 Appropriation Bill, valued at N1,115,341,378,359.94, before lawmakers at the Parliament Building, Secretariat, Ibadan. Speaking against the backdrop of recent resignations by political appointees and other government officials, Makinde said he was keeping count of those who had left but insisted that their decisions were of no significance to his administration. He also disclosed that one of the female officials who resigned had approached him with what he described as an impossible request, adding that she tendered her resignation after he declined to grant it. The presentation is particularly significant as the proposed estimates represent the final appropriation bill of Makinde’s administration, which is expected to complete its second term in 2027. Under the proposal, capital expenditure accounts for N670.03 billion, representing 60.07 per cent of the total budget, while recurrent expenditure stands at N445.31 billion, or 39.93 per cent. Explaining the allocation, the governor said the proposed spending reflected his administration’s determination to sustain infrastructure development, consolidate existing achievements and strengthen the delivery of essential services across the state. He said about 60 per cent of every N100 provided for in the budget would go into capital investments, stressing that infrastructure remained central to economic growth and long-term prosperity. Makinde, however, cautioned that physical infrastructure alone could not guarantee meaningful development without adequate investment in human resources and essential public services. He said schools needed teachers, hospitals required healthcare professionals, medicines and equipment, while public institutions must be adequately staffed and equipped to function effectively. According to him, the proposed budget was also informed by consultations with stakeholders and residents across the state’s administrative and political zones, whose concerns and expectations shaped the government’s spending priorities. The governor also used the occasion to advocate continuity in governance beyond the expiration of his tenure, unveiling what he called the Omituntun 3.0 agenda. He said the initiative was designed to prevent a reversal of the development trajectory established by his administration over the past seven and a half years after the 2027 governorship election. item.title: Carex Rewards Thousands Of Consumers As Everybody Wins Promo Concludes With Grand Finale Live Draw
item.description: Carex, one of Nigeria’s leading personal hygiene brands, has successfully concluded its nationwide Everybody Wins Promo with a transparent Grand Finale Live Draw, rewarding loyal consumers and reinforcing its commitment to delivering value beyond personal care products. The campaign, which ran from June 2026 to August 2026, attracted millions of consumers PAN Nigeria and rewarded winners with prizes worth over ₦400,000,000. The Grand Finale Live Draw, held in Lagos, brought together consumers, media representatives, trade partners, regulatory officials, and other key stakeholders to witness the selection of the campaign’s grand prize winner through a transparent and independently supervised process. The event marked the culmination of months of consumer participation and engagement, further strengthening the connection between the Carex brand and its consumers. Throughout the promotion, participants had multiple opportunities to win exciting rewards, including instant Recharge Cards, shopping Vouchers, and a brand-new Car. Over 90,000 consumers emerged as winners over the course of the campaign. The grand prize car winner, Faith Stephen from Ijebu Ode, Ogun State, emerged through the live draw process conducted in accordance with all applicable promotional and regulatory requirements. Speaking at the event, Ifunanya Anwunah, Head of Category – Personal Hygiene, said: “At Carex, we believe that the consumers who trust our products every day deserve to be appreciated and rewarded. The Everybody Wins Promo was created as a tangible expression of our gratitude for the loyalty and support we continue to receive from Nigerian families. The overwhelming participation and enthusiasm witnessed throughout this campaign demonstrate the strong connection consumers have with the Carex brand. The promo was built on a simple promise: giving everyday consumers the opportunity to win meaningful rewards while enjoying the quality, care, and protection they have come to trust from Carex. As a brand trusted by millions of Nigerians for their personal hygiene and care needs, Carex remains committed to developing initiatives that deepen consumer engagement, reward loyalty, and create memorable experiences for consumers across the country. The successful completion of the Everybody Wins Promo further underscores the brand’s commitment to putting consumers at the heart of everything it does. ABOUT CAREX Carex is committed to winning the war against germs through a range of antibacterial products that support the health, hygiene, and wellbeing of consumers. Through innovative products and engaging consumer initiatives, Carex continues to build meaningful connections with families across Nigeria, delivering trusted products that help consumers live healthier and more confident lives. The post Carex Rewards Thousands Of Consumers As Everybody Wins Promo Concludes With Grand Finale Live Draw appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: One of our favorite multi-filament 3D printers is $100 off
item.description: The Bambu P2S Combo. | Image: Bambu If you’re tired of filament jams and clogged nozzles, perhaps it’s time for a new 3D printer. Through December 1st, the Bambu Lab P2S Combo , currently one of the best models that’s easy to use, is discounted. It’s $649 at Best Buy, as well as directly from Bambu Lab . That’s $100 off the list price for the bundle, which includes the Bambu P2S printer and the AMS 2 Pro multi-filament handler for multicolor prints. Bambu Lab P2S Combo Bambu Lab’s P2S is a 3D printer with a 5-inch touchscreen and a built-in camera that lets you monitor your prints remotely. It also uses AI to detect printing problems. Where to Buy: $779 at Amazon $749.99 $649.99 at Best Buy $749 $649 at Bambu Lab My colleague Sean Hollister praised the P2S printer for its consistency and hands-off approach to 3D printing. Automatic bed leveling, including a warning if you forget to reinstall the plate, and a bevy of sensors helps ensure every print goes smoothly. There’s a live camera feed, too, so you can check in on your prints or share a timelapse. On its own, the P2S printer is usually $549, but is also currently $100 off. The AMS 2 Pro’s filament handler’s fully enclosed setup saves your filament from absorbing moisture and clogging the nozzle or tubes. As a result, you can go weeks between prints and fire one off from your computer without checking on colors or manually swapping filaments. The AMS 2 Pro itself is typically $299, but is currently on sale for $229, and the P2S printer supports up to four AMS 2 Pro units simultaneously. Read our Bambu P2S review .

item.title: ADC-PCC to Tinubu: Where is the electricity you promised Nigerians?
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for his unfulfilled electricity pledge, accusing him of resorting to personal attacks, divisive rhetoric and recycled promises instead of presenting a credible scorecard of his administration. The Council said Nigerians expected the President to explain what had become of his major campaign promises after nearly three-and-a-half years in office, particularly against the backdrop of worsening insecurity, widespread hunger, rising living costs and massive government borrowings. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC said Tinubu’s recent campaign outings in Kaduna, Rivers and Jigawa states offered little beyond verbal attacks on opponents and familiar promises. Recalling the President’s electricity pledge, the Council challenged him to explain why millions of Nigerians were still struggling with unreliable power supply. “If I don’t give you electricity, don’t vote for me for a second term,” it quoted Tinubu as saying. The ADC-PCC described his renewed electricity promises during the Jigawa campaign as an attempt to repackage an old commitment, adding that the President had reportedly invested in alternative power arrangements for his personal comfort. The Council also questioned the fate of 2,000 tractors reportedly imported from Brazil under the administration’s mechanised farming initiative, alleging that they had yet to make any meaningful impact on agricultural productivity. It further accused Tinubu of taking credit for projects initiated by his predecessor, late President Muhammadu Buhari, insisting that his administration had little of its own to showcase. On the state of democracy, the ADC-PCC accused the President of undermining the independence of democratic institutions, alleging undue influence over the National Assembly and attempts to compromise the Judiciary. It also took issue with Tinubu’s declaration that ‘all is fair in politics’. warning that such a position could encourage political illegality, intimidation, violence and thuggery. The Council said: “The opposition is increasingly confronted with unconstitutional conduct, judicial rascality, political intimidation and a compromised electoral environment under the APC administration.” Citing the President’s recent campaign outing in Rivers State, the ADC-PCC questioned his decision to praise and promise to reward a political figure whom it alleged had been illegally removed from office, denied political participation for six months and prevented from seeking re-election. “Reward him for what?” Ologbondiyan queried, describing the President’s conduct as an affront to constitutional governance and the democratic rights of the people. item.title: 14-year-old creates tool for AI agents to band together like a team
item.description: Built by a 14-year-old developer, a new tool called Autark treats AI agents as a virtual team that can work without constant prompting. Users put tasks in an inbox, where a manager agent delegates them to other agents that carry out the work and report their results. Agents can also ask clarifying questions if tasks are too vague. “Agents do not wait for a prompt,” Autark’s website explains . “A schedule, a timer, a new task, a message or an event wakes them up. They decide what to do, do it, and can plan their own next step.” As one would hope from a product like this, Autark is model agnostic and can be set up to connect to OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Kimi Code through those services’ CLI tools. Local models are also supported. Your mileage may vary if you choose to use anything besides Codex or Claude Code, though, as Autark’s website mentions support for other models is built in but hasn’t been tested in a live run yet, as Autark is still under active development as an open-source tool. Real teenage engineering Autark is the brainchild of teenage Austrian developer Stanislaus Hees. He’s still in school, and tells The Register he’s deeply interested in AI and came up with Autark after being unhappy with existing AI tools. “I could get help with individual tasks, but I still had to organise the work, remember what was unfinished and keep pushing it forward,” Hees said of his time using Claude Code and Codex. “I wanted a system that could take responsibility for ongoing work, not just respond to my next message.” He developed Autark - or, more accurately, prompted AI coding tools to do it for him - to come up with a tool that could fulfill that want. You know what that means: It’s capable, but that capability also makes it dangerous. Autark’s page on access and data makes clear what’s at risk if you give it unfettered access to a PC, and why you don’t want to let the thing run roughshod over a system. “It can do everything,” the page explains , because “Autark does not put walls around its agents.” There’s no sandboxing in Autark, no approval prompts, and no permission gates. It doesn’t stop agents from spending all the money they can get their hands on, deleting files, or sending unsolicited emails, either. Agents run with the privileges of the machine's user, with approval checks and permission restrictions disabled or bypassed. Even the safety limit parley that users have with Autark establishes guidelines, not rules. “The first thing the AI asks is how far it may go,” the access page points out. “That is a question, not a technical barrier.” That means agents given a task that conflicts with their stated limits may still attempt to carry it out. As we’ve seen in recent months , some AI agents have found ways around restrictions, instructions be damned. “In our own live test runs, agents given a vague request reached real repositories, backups, SSH keys and .env files within minutes, and one changed the perm

item.title: N210trn not missing from NNPC – Mele Kyari tells Senate
item.description: By Henry Umoru – ABUJA The immediate past Group Chief Executive Officer, GCEO, of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company, NNPC, Limited, Mele Kyari has appeared before the Senate, refuting alleged unaccounted N210 trillion in the balance sheet of the National oil company as contained in the 2017 to 2023 Audit report. Kyari who finally appeared before the Senator Ibrahim Dankwabo (PDP, Gombe North) led Senate Committee on Public Accounts said the alleged unaccounted figures arose from accounting entries which have nothing to do with financial loss. He declared that no such financial infraction happened under him as Chief Executive of NNPCL from 2019 to 2025. Kyari said, “I wish to confirm that nothing was lost. It is simply not possible that such an amount could have been lost under my care and leadership. “The matter relates to accounting entries, which have nothing to do with any financial loss. “They are bookkeeping issues, and I believe the appropriate explanations have been provided in my report.” The former NNPCL boss who declared that the N5billion allegedly spent on change of name from NNPC to NNPCL , waa untrue as there was no spending like that under his watch, however refuted queries raised in the audit report on registration and incorporation of NNPC Ltd. He said: “At the time of incorporation, the company was not owned by the Federation in the same manner. “The Federation was therefore responsible for the payment relating to the incorporation of NNPC. “However, NNPC made the payment on behalf of the Federation and subsequently charged it to the Federation’s revenue, which was reflected in what we referred to as the former NAPIMS account of NNPC. “This was simply an accounting entry, involving approximately N2.99 billion. It was a payment made to government institutions responsible for providing the relevant services. “I have also seen comments suggesting that N5 billion was paid for the naming of the company. That is not correct”. According to him, NNPCL under him was transformed from loss incurring corporation to a profit making company, adding that prior to his assumption of office as Group Managing Director of NNPC in 2019 , the national oil company had a huge loss of $803billion in 2018 operational year , which gradually turned to o profit making under him from 2019 . Kyari said, “Mr Chairman, you may be aware from the financial records that the company recorded a loss of about $803billion in 2018. “I took over in 2019, and we did everything possible to transform the company into a profitable organisation which made it to for the first time in its 44 years of existence, recording sustained profits” Satisfied with the submissions of Kyari , the Committee through its Chairman, Senator Dankwabo said , responses submitted to the queries shall be thoroughly studied for final decision on the audit report . item.title: ACF crisis deepens as chairman alleges invasion of secretariat
item.description: — Osuman accuses individuals of breaking into Kaduna headquarters, removing valuables By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The leadership crisis in the Arewa Consultative Forum (ACF) has taken a fresh turn following allegations by its National Chairman, Maman Mike Osuman, that some individuals forcibly gained access to the organisation’s national secretariat in Kaduna and removed valuables. In a petition dated November 9, 2026, and addressed to Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State, Osuman accused two individuals of allegedly breaking into the ACF headquarters at No. 11A Sokoto Road, Kaduna, without the authorisation of the recognised leadership. The petition was also copied to the Inspector-General of Police, the Kaduna State Commissioner of Police and the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) in the state. According to Osuman, the individuals allegedly gained access to the premises by breaking the gates and office doors, changing the locks and removing valuables and other properties belonging to the organisation. He further alleged that the operation was carried out without the knowledge or consent of the recognised leadership of the forum and without a search warrant. Describing the alleged incident as an assault on the institutional integrity of the organisation, Osuman appealed to Governor Sani to intervene to prevent further escalation of the crisis. “An invasion of this nature not only violates the sanctity of our corporate headquarters but is also a direct assault on the dignity of the entire Northern Region,” he said. The chairman described the national secretariat as the collective heritage of Northern Nigeria, stressing that its protection was essential to preserving the dignity and integrity of the organisation. He urged the governor to use his good offices to ensure that the rule of law prevailed and that the forum was protected against actions capable of undermining its stability. The latest allegation has renewed attention on the protracted leadership crisis within the ACF, particularly the disagreement over control of its national secretariat and the authority to manage the organisation’s affairs. The dispute has been characterised by competing positions among the forum’s leadership organs over the interpretation of its constitution, leadership structure and the legitimacy of decisions taken by the contending sides. In one of the major developments, the National Executive Committee (NEC) of the forum reportedly suspended its Board of Trustees (BoT) Chairman, Alhaji Bashir M. Dalhatu, over alleged violations of the organisation’s constitution. The suspension followed an emergency NEC meeting held in Kaduna in May 2026, amid tensions over access to the ACF headquarters and reports of police restrictions ahead of the meeting. However, the Board of Trustees subsequently rejected Dalhatu’s purported suspension, describing the decision as illegal and unconstitutional and an attempt to destabilise the northern socio-cultural organisation. item.title: 2027: Stakeholders demand action against electoral violence
item.description: … Falana urges INEC prosecution unit, police warn politicians against sponsoring thugs By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Stakeholders have called for stricter enforcement of electoral laws, prosecution of offenders and accountability for political actors to curb violence ahead of the 2027 general elections. They made the call at the sixth edition of the Frontier Discourse Annual Public Lecture Series and Awards, organised by Pacesetter Frontier Magazine in Abuja on Tuesday, where speakers expressed concern over political thuggery, restrictions on opposition campaigns, unemployment, insecurity and the failure to enforce laws protecting citizens. The event was themed, “Barrel to Ballot: The Naturalisation of Violence, Nigeria’s Polity, and its Democratic Circus.” Delivering the keynote address, human rights lawyer and Senior Advocate of Nigeria, Femi Falana, urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to establish a dedicated prosecution unit to handle electoral offences. He said the commission should obtain reports from the police and other security agencies, investigate electoral violations and prosecute those found culpable. Falana argued that the Electoral Act placed responsibility for prosecuting electoral offenders on INEC, insisting that the commission should not leave the task entirely to the police and other security agencies. He also faulted the National Assembly for failing to implement the recommendation for the establishment of an Electoral Offences Commission, alleging that politicians were deliberately allowing a system that encouraged political thuggery to persist. The senior advocate warned against portraying political violence as the exclusive preserve of any political party, saying supporters of both the ruling party and opposition parties had been involved in attacks. “I am suggesting that INEC should have a prosecution unit with a view to getting reports from the police and other security agencies about electoral offences and then take them to court,” he said. “The politicians in Abuja, members of the National Assembly have refused, deliberately so, to implement the recommendation that there shall be in the country an electoral offences commission. “Politicians do not want to distort the status quo. So they want us to continue to live with thuggery because the thugs are agents of politicians from all the political spectrum.” Falana also alleged that opposition parties had been prevented from erecting campaign billboards in some states, while supporters of different political parties had engaged in acts of vandalism and attacks against their opponents. He insisted that no political party should be allowed to claim innocence or justify violence against its opponents, stressing that all political actors must be held accountable. He further criticised state governments for allegedly imposing excessive charges on campaign billboards, saying some had introduced guidelines capable of restricting opposition parties’ access to camp

item.title: Mozilla Thunderbird email service edges closer to launch with early access
item.description: The Mozilla-backed Thunderbird project is getting closer to a wider launch of a hosted email service designed to complement its desktop mail app. Now known as Thundermail (what else?), the service was originally developed under the Thunderbird Pro banner, which encompassed paid email, appointment scheduling, and file-sharing services designed to generate additional revenue for the organization. The org has been inviting people from its Thundermail waitlist to try the service through an early-access program, and this writer just happened to be among them. Thundermail offers a web-based email interface and can also be accessed through the Thunderbird desktop app, the Thunderbird mobile app for Android, or other compatible email clients. The Thunderbird apps remain free. Users get an inbox with up to 15 email addresses and three custom domains, plus 30 GB of mail storage and 60 GB of send storage for Thunderbird Send, an end-to-end encrypted file-sharing and large-attachment service. That’s for starters – the org intends to offer those extra features and services at different price points. Yes, Thundermail is a paid service, which may put off some users who are used to free email accounts offered via Gmail, Outlook.com and Proton Mail, but with the first two of those you do get served ads along with your messages. The sign-up screens for Thundermail suggest the basic service will cost $6 per month, billed annually. This is roughly equivalent to the £55 we paid for a year on the early access program. We asked Thunderbird when we can expect to see Thundermail officially launched and open to all comers. We will update if we get an answer. It previously said that a full launch is expected sometime in 2026. The web-based user interface of Thundermail presents a fairly clean and uncluttered look, and could be likened to Gmail with the screen partitioned into a pane with folders on the left and a larger one to the right displaying messages. A welcome screen introduces you to the features of Thundermail, which include the ability to work on several drafts at once, schedule delivery times for emails, create folders to arrange messages, contact lists and identities – all pretty much standard for an email system. We haven’t really had the time to test out Thundermail a great deal since signing up, but there are no great surprises so far, and everything works pretty much the way you would expect it to. Firefox and the Thunderbird mail client both recently moved to a fortnightly release schedule in line with Mozilla’s plans, and Thunderbird itself gained support for Microsoft’s Exchange late last year. ®

item.title: Bagudu: With Tinubu’s reforms, prosperity is guaranteed
item.description: Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Bagudu, has said the difficult times brought about by President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms are over, paving the way for assured shared prosperity for Nigerians. The minister spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the media presentation of the All Progressives Congress 2027 presidential election manifesto, themed “From Reforms to Prosperity,” which outlines the Tinubu administration’s policy direction and commitments to translating ongoing reforms into improved living conditions for Nigerians. Bagudu said President Tinubu’s reforms have strengthened private-sector confidence, attracted investment and laid the foundation for inclusive prosperity. He recalled the economic challenges faced by state governments in 2015, when several governors reportedly struggled to meet salary obligations, and contrasted that period with what he described as increased federal allocations, sustained economic growth and improving investor confidence. Bagudu, however, stressed that the ultimate measure of the reforms would be their impact on ordinary Nigerians, particularly hardworking citizens and vulnerable households, and said the next four years of President Tinubu’s tenure will be dedicated to ensuring the people feel the positive impact of the reforms. Also speaking at the presentation, the Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, described the manifesto as a social contract between the government and Nigerians, emphasising that its commitments must be measurable and accountable. He acknowledged the economic pressures of removing the fuel subsidy and implementing foreign exchange reforms, but maintained that the administration’s responsibility was to ensure the gains from reform translate into a better quality of life. L-R: Member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Abdulmumin Jibrin; Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Abubakar Bagudu; Minister of Industry, Trade, and Investment, Dr Jumoke Oduwole; Chief of Staff to the President, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila; Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake; Minister of Information and National Orientation, Alhaji Mohammed Idris; and Minister of Steel Development, Mr Shuaibu Audu, at the presentation of the APC 2027 General Election Manifesto in Abuja on Tuesday 10/11/26 He highlighted initiatives including the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), tax reforms and the Electricity Act, alongside manifesto commitments to halve the number of out-of-school children by 2031, provide seven million additional electricity meters and expand access to health insurance. item.title: NASA to Welcome Expedition 74 Astronauts Home at Space Center Houston
item.description: (March 15, 2026) — The International Space Station orbits 267 miles above a cloudy Atlantic Ocean southwest of Cape Town, South Africa. The Kibo laboratory module’s External Platform and the Canadarm2 robotic arm highlight the top foreground above Earth’s terminator—the line between night and day—in this photograph taken at approximately 6:36 a.m. local time. Credit: ESA/Sophie Adenot NASA will welcome home the Expedition 74 crew during a public event at Space Center Houston following their return from a long-duration mission aboard the International Space Station. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams; ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot; and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud‑Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev will share mission highlights at 6 p.m. CST Tuesday, Nov. 17, at NASA Johnson Space Center’s visitor center. An awards ceremony recognizing key mission contributors will follow the presentation. The astronauts will be available for media interviews before the event. Media may request an in-person interview no later than 5 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16, by emailing the JSC Newsroom at jsc-newsroom@mail.nasa.gov . Williams, Kud‑Sverchkov, and Mikaev launched aboard the Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan on Nov. 27, 2025. The trio returned to Earth on July 26, making a parachute-assisted landing southeast of Dzhezkazgan, Kazakhstan. The crew was in space for 241 days, orbiting the Earth 3,856 times and traveling more than 102 million miles. The mission was the first for Williams and Mikaev and the second for Kud-Sverchkov. Meir, Hathaway, and Adenot launched aboard a Dragon spacecraft on Feb. 13 as part of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 mission from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. After more than seven months aboard the space station, Meir, Hathaway, and Adenot safely splashed down on Oct. 8 in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles. During their 237-day mission, the four crew members traveled more than 100 million miles and completed more than 3,792 orbits around Earth. The mission was the second for Meir and the first for Hathaway and Adenot. Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev also flew as part of Crew-12 but is unavailable for the event. The Expedition 74 crew dedicated more than 1,400 hours to scientific research and technology demonstrations aboard the International Space Station. Its work advanced in-space manufacturing by testing metal and tissue 3D-printing technologies and supported human health studies examining the effects of long-duration spaceflight. Research included blood flow studies, assessments of piloting capabilities under changing gravitational conditions, and activation of a new compact exercise system . The crew also evaluated life-support and environmental systems critical to future exploration missions under NASA’s Artemis program. item.title: Nigeria’s Danielle Adewusi Begins Her Miss Universe 2026 Journey in Puerto Rico
item.description: Danielle Adewusi in a custom off-white and burgundy ensemble featuring gold embroidery and a dramatic train for her Miss Universe departure. Photo Credit: Danielle Adewusi/Instagram The road to the 75th Miss Universe crown is officially underway, and Nigeria’s representative, Dr Danielle Adewusi , has touched down in San Juan, Puerto Rico, to begin pre-pageant activities. Danielle was crowned Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 on 27 September at the Balmoral Hall, Federal Palace Hotel in Lagos. Competing as Miss Lagos State against 19 other delegates, her victory marked a full-circle moment: her mother won the national title in 1991, 35 years before her. An alumnus of King’s College London, Danielle holds an MBBS alongside a first-class honours degree in Psychology. Alongside her medical career, she leads Scrub the Stigma, an initiative focused on expanding healthcare access and raising awareness around women’s health across Nigeria and the UK. Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 Danielle Adewusi wearing her official national crown and gold sequin gown. Photo Credit: Danielle Adewusi/Instagram Before taking the national crown, she placed in the Top 5 at Miss Universe Great Britain in 2023 and completed international runway coaching in Thailand. With recent updates by the Miss Universe Organisation removing maximum age limits, 29-year-old Danielle is also among the delegates competing under the expanded eligibility rules. Arriving in San Juan on Monday, 9 November, Danielle joins nearly 120 delegates from across the globe for preliminary rounds, national costume presentations, and rehearsals. The grand finale of the 75th Miss Universe pageant takes place on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot in San Juan. Danielle Adewusi waves the Nigerian flag at the airport as she departs for the Miss Universe 2026 pageant in Puerto Rico. item.title: Steam Deck performance gets a reality check with Valve's new FPS data
item.description: Since Valve announced its Steam Deck Verified program in 2021 , players have found that a game's "Verified" status doesn't always match how well it actually runs on the handheld. Now, new Steam Deck frame rate data being shared by Valve itself can help players dig deeper into the performance they can expect from many Steam Deck games. Valve has been collecting anonymized frame rate data from Steam players who opt in since February . Yesterday evening, the company announced it has started sharing that data on many Steam Store pages as averages and histograms for both the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED. Valve acknowledges that players enabling VSync or frame rate limits can bias the collected data somewhat and that the measurements don't account for custom in-game settings that Steam Deck users may tinker with to get a game running. Regardless, Valve says it has nonetheless "found that the framerate data consolidates around relatively narrow ranges." Read full article Comments

item.title: AMD winds up Zen 6 cores for faster clock speeds
item.description: After teasing its 256-core Epycs for more than a year, AMD is finally ready to talk about architectural changes to the Zen core that not only make it possible, but will eventually power its next generation of Ryzen processors in desktop and mobile PCs. During a press event in Las Vegas last week, AMD spilled the beans on its latest Zen cores, which promise an average 27 percent uplift in instructions per clock (IPC) across a variety of AI and server workloads, along with boosted clocks ranging from 4.1 to 5.3 GHz. We expect to see even higher frequencies on consumer chips before long, but AMD isn’t quite ready to talk about Ryzen just yet. CPU performance is a function of power, IPC, and clocks, and with gains across all three, the cores are shaping up to be one of the company’s biggest generational jumps ever. A tale of two cores As in past Epyc launches, Zen 6 isn’t one core. It comes in two flavors: a frequency-optimized variant (Zen 6) and a density-optimized version (Zen 6c). This split dates back to the launch of AMD’s Bergamo Epycs in 2023, which packed 128 compact Zen 4c cores into just eight chiplets. The chip’s debut drew comparisons to Intel’s still relatively new Efficient (E-cores) for obvious reasons. But under the hood, AMD’s Zen 4c was nothing like what Intel was doing. The core itself was nearly identical to Zen 4; it simply traded clocks and a bit of cache per core for a more densely packed CPU die. The only difference between running an application on Bergamo or Genoa was how quickly it executed. The same could not be said of Intel’s P and E cores, which used different ISAs. This remained a defining characteristic and advantage of AMD’s compact core architecture through Zen 5, which allowed it to ship Turin parts with up to 192 cores without users having to worry about whether their app was running on a compact core or not. With Zen 6c, at least as we understand it, this philosophy is largely unchanged. Both Zen 6 and Zen 6c share the same ISA, with clock being the main differentiator. There are other micro-architectural differences between the two cores designed to balance IPC and clock speeds more effectively. Looking at the core’s block diagram, this isn’t immediately obvious. Zen 6 and Zen 5 share a very similar front and backend. We'd be tempted to call the core iterative if it weren't for the 20 to 31 percent IPC uplift for cloud and AI workloads that AMD claims over Zen 5. This suggests that core for core, a 4.1 GHz Zen 6c-based Venice Epyc should deliver performance on par with a Zen 5-based Turin Epyc running at 5 GHz. That's a pretty sizable jump, but just because AMD is seeing generational performance uplift in enterprise server and cloud workloads doesn't mean we'll see the same gains on the client side. Many will recall the roughly 5 percent performance gains gaming PC enthusiasts reported with the Ryzen 9000-series, leading to the rather unfortunate turn of phrase "Zen 5 percent." item.title: Canaan (CAN) Swings to an $8 Million Profit on Bitcoin Gains as Rig Sales Collapse 96%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Canaan (CAN) Swings to an $8 Million Profit on Bitcoin Gains as Rig Sales Collapse 96% Canaan Inc. (NASDAQ: CAN) swung to $8.0 million of third-quarter net income on a $51.9 million fair-value gain in its bitcoin holdings and derivatives, the mining-rig maker said Tuesday, even as machine sales collapsed 96%. The company filed the unaudited results Tuesday in a 6-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Total revenue fell to $14.5 million from $150.5 million a year earlier, including $4.8 million from product sales and $9.5 million from mining. Canaan sold 1.0 million terahashes per second of computing power and mined 133 bitcoin. The profit did not come from the business. Canaan posted an $8.6 million gross loss and a $42.9 million operating loss. Chief financial officer Jin “James” Cheng said a recovery in bitcoin prices toward quarter-end generated the $51.9 million fair-value gain and called it “distinct from underlying operating performance.” The $51.9 million is the sum of a $20.1 million gain on cryptocurrency and a $31.9 million gain on financial derivatives. Canaan also reported $22.4 million of non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, a figure that still includes those gains. Strip them out and adjusted EBITDA would have been a loss of about $29.5 million. Nangeng Zhang, Canaan’s chairman and chief executive officer, pointed to “continued weakness in bitcoin mining equipment demand and intense industry pricing competition.” Products revenue dropped from $13.6 million in the second quarter and from $118.6 million in the same period of 2025. The company blamed lower volumes and a lower average selling price. The treasury carries the quarter Canaan took $8.2 million of inventory-related write-downs, down from $25.3 million in the second quarter. Mining operations posted a gross margin of about 30% before depreciation, with an all-in power cost of about $0.043 per kilowatt-hour and roughly 10 exahashes per second of installed capacity outside joint ventures. The company held 1,875.5 bitcoin as of Sept. 30. Of that, 517.5 coins were owned outright, 1,258 were pledged for secured term loans and 100 sat in a fixed-term product. It booked $43.7 million of cryptocurrency assets and $114.2 million of cryptocurrency receivables. The stack is down about 40 bitcoin from the 1,915.5 Canaan reported at the end of the second quarter, even after the company mined 133 in the period, implying it moved roughly 173 bitcoin off the treasury. Zhang said Canaan is “selectively monetizing cryptocurrency holdings to fund share repurchases.” On Nov. 6, the board approved a new $100 million share repurchase authorization over 12 months and launched an initial $20 million program under that cap. A 2-gigawatt Texas bet, and a reverse split Canaan is trying to recast itself around power and compute infrastructure. item.title: AMD's Epyc X-chips are back after a three-year hiatus
item.description: AMD's cache-packed Epyc X chips are officially making a comeback. Based on the House of Zen's frequency-optimized SKUs we looked at back in September , its HPC-optimized Venice-X parts will offer up to 96 cores and use the company's 3D V-Cache chip stack tech to triple the L3 cache density to more than a gigabyte. But before you get too excited about another cache-packed Epyc, it'll be a little while before they actually ship. AMD expects the Venice-X to begin trickling out in the second half of 2027. First teased at CES earlier this year, the chips are primarily aimed at latency-sensitive technical and scientific computing workloads like computational fluid dynamics and electronic design automation (EDA). AMD itself relies heavily on its X-series Epycs for EDA workloads like functional verification testing, which is used to simulate silicon in order to ensure it behaves as it's intended to. According to AMD Fellow Phil Steinke, by keeping more of the model in cache, the CPU cores don't have to wait as long for data to move in and out of system memory. Normally, boosting L3 capacity would have required larger chiplets with lower yields, but that's not how AMD has gone about it for the past four years. Instead, it used advanced packaging to give its existing CPU dies a little SRAM backpack. This tech has been around for several generations now, having first debuted in the Ryzen 7 5800X3D back in 2022. That consumer desktop chip stacked a 64 MB SRAM tile on top of an 8-core chiplet, boosting L3 capacity to 96 MB. The extra cache made the chip one of the most potent gaming CPUs of the time. Later that year, AMD brought the same technology to its Milan generation of Epycs as the company expanded its portfolio to address a wider range of workloads. The extra cache was popular enough to justify a second generation of X-series Epycs, which launched in 2023. But then, nothing. When AMD unveiled its 5th-gen Epycs in late 2024, there was no Turin-X on the roadmap. According to Madhu Rangarajan, who runs AMD's compute and enterprise AI products biz, this was intentional. "We are not doing the X every generation.... The enterprise HPC kind of market tends to have a cadence that's a little bit slower, so that's what drives our cadence." Venice-X marks the return of AMD's X-chips, and for the most part, the processor largely follows the same recipe as its predecessors. Each of the chip's up to eight CPU dies is now bonded to a 96 MB SRAM tile using advanced packaging, for a total of 144 MB of L3 per chiplet or 1,152 MB per socket, which you might have noticed is the same as in the Genoa-X parts they replace. But while core count and cache capacity haven't increased, clock speeds certainly have, with Venice now hitting 5.3 GHz compared to Genoa-X at just 3.7 GHz. "In Milan and Genoa, there was one trade-off. You either had to choose something that was high frequency or you chose something with 3D V-Cache." HPC likes both, Rangarajan told El Reg . item.title: Were there 'lost cosmonauts' in the early Soviet space program?
item.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

In the final weeks of 1960, two young radio enthusiasts were monitoring transmissions from a home-built listening station on a rooftop in Turin, Italy, when the brothers detected something extraordinary: a faint signal that bore the hallmarks of one originating from space. That wasn't the only surprising thing about the alleged signal:, the transmission carried a very familiar message: it was Morse code for the international distress signal SOS. As the youths listened, the signal seemed to grow weaker. This raised a troubling possibility: could it be that the signal's source was moving farther away from Earth ? And if so, was it possible that this concerning signal was of Soviet origin — perhaps a spacecraft drifting helplessly into space, carrying a cosmonaut on board whose doomed mission had never been publicly acknowledged? These strange events from November 1960 became the first in a series of alleged radio signal interceptions that would form the basis of an enduring Cold War-era mystery involving so-called "lost cosmonauts" — early Soviet space travelers rumored to have died during secret spaceflight missions before Yuri Gagarin's historic flight the following spring, in April 1961.Today, more than six decades later, the story remains one of the most haunting legends of the Space Age. Were there truly early Soviet space missions — with tragically ill-fated cosmonaut crews — that remain undisclosed to this day? Interception at Torre Bert The peculiar story began in October 1957, as the Italian brothers Achille and Gian Battista Judica-Cordiglia learned, along with the rest of the world, about the Soviet Union's successful launch of Sputnik 1 , Earth's first artificial satellite. Immediately, the two became fascinated with the idea of trying to listen in on signals from such spacecraft and began working to assemble their very own radio tracking station, which they put together mostly from secondhand military surplus equipment. What they couldn't easily find and purchase, the brothers would often assemble themselves. They built an improvised tracking station in an abandoned World War Two bunker , which the brothers dubbed Torre Bert, that eventually became a fully functional radio facility with an antenna they built from salvaged materials like chicken wire and scraps of metal. The Judica-Cordiglia brothers, Achille (left) and Giovanni Battista (right). (Image credit: Public domain) Whatever it lacked in aesthetics, the station made up for in functionality, and soon the brothers' amateur efforts reportedly allowed them to successfully intercept transmissions associated with Sputnik 2 , the first Soviet spacecraft to carry a living creature into orbit: a dog named Laika , who became a o

item.title: A closer look at Verano, AMD's first step toward a Zen-based superchip to rival Nvidia's Vera Rubin
item.description: AMD's upcoming Verano processors aren't like any Epyc CPUs we've seen before. Rather than general-purpose workloads, Verano is designed specifically to power AMD's next generation of GPU servers. In an interview with The Register during a press event in Las Vegas last week, Madhu Rangarajan, CVP of AMD's compute and enterprise AI products business, described Verano as being the first step towards building something that more closely resembles Nvidia's Vera Rubin superchips. "Verano is really designed for an integrated CPU+GPU rack scale solution," he said. "From that perspective, I wouldn't say the CPU is a competitor to Vera. In a head note, I'd say the Verano+GPU solution is a competitor to Vera+Rubin." For reference, Vera Rubin and the GB200 and GB300 that came before it aren't your typical server platforms. Instead they're more like an enormous single-board computer combining CPUs and GPUs into a tightly-integrated package. Each of Nvidia's superchips joins a single 88-core Vera CPU and 1.5 TB of LPDDR5X memory to a pair of Rubin GPUs via Nvidia's speedy NVLink-C2C interconnect. Rangarajan tells us Verano will be the host CPU for a similar class of product using AMD GPUs, and much like Nvidia's superchips, the CPU will also use notebook memory rather than conventional RDIMMS. However, unlike Vera, which is also being deployed as a standalone CPU in storage servers and agent sandboxes, Verano has a singular purpose: keeping its GPUs fed. (We assume they'll be MI500X GPUs.) This design choice reflects AMD's philosophy of one SKU per workload. As such, Verano's core count, clock speeds, memory bandwidth, power, and I/O have been rebalanced to keep its GPUs fed and not much else. Under the hood If we were to peel back Verano's heat spreader, the chip looks a lot like the Venice Epycs we looked at back in September. It features either six of AMD's core complex dies (CCDs) for a total of 72 high-frequency cores clocking to 5.3 GHz, or 192 density-optimized cores clocking to 4.1 GHz, depending on whether the customer's workloads prefer core density or faster clocks. But that's about where the visual similarities end. Much of the chip has been reworked to eliminate data flow bottlenecks between the CPU and the GPUs it is responsible for feeding. The chip features an entirely custom pair of I/O dies through which four LPDDR5X memory controllers are attached. Those memory controllers are currently being validated for use with 24 channels of memory at up to 8,533 MT/s. We're told that we may see that creep up a bit depending on how much headroom AMD has when the part starts shipping next year, but for now that's what AMD is validating against. That means the platform not only has fewer cores, but also slower memory. Peak theoretical memory bandwidth tops out at around 800 GB/s, which you might have noticed is half of what AMD's top-specced Venice parts can do and about 66 percent of Nvidia's Vera. What LPDDR seems to buy AMD is a 30 to 40 percent reduct

item.title: Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent Binance warned iPhone users Tuesday that a publicly released iOS flaw could let malicious apps read files stored by other apps, including the seed phrases and private keys that control crypto wallets. “A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem,” the exchange wrote on X. “This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.” Binance told users to delete any apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed IPA files, and to update iOS and every app to the latest official versions. Anyone who suspects a breach should move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions, the exchange said. Neither Binance nor the researcher behind the flaw has reported any thefts tied to it. What worse_query does The bug is a sandbox escape. On iOS, each app is supposed to live in its own container that other apps cannot read. A researcher who posts as forcequitOS released worse_query on GitHub on Nov. 8, calling it “a zero-day sandbox escape for iOS 26 and 27, again.” It succeeds an earlier exploit, bad_query. The project’s README says it works on iOS 26.0 through 26.7.2 and on iOS 27.2, a wider range than the versions Binance named. It lists paths it can reach, including other apps’ data containers and shared app group folders. The researcher describes it as “a proof-of-concept for developers” that “isn’t useful by itself,” and stresses it is not a jailbreak. To use it, a developer has to build it into an app. That has already happened in at least one case. A day after the release, developer Christoph Kolbicz published a file manager built on worse_query that lets users browse and edit app data on iOS 27 without jailbreaking, which he said was tested on iOS 27.0.1. Blockchain security firm SlowMist called worse_query a container sandbox escape rather than a jailbreak. Its chief information security officer, who posts as 23pds, wrote that the flaw will not steal assets on its own. The risk comes when a user installs and runs an untrusted IPA that then reads other apps’ containers, and only if a wallet stores mnemonic phrases, keystores or WebView caches in plain text on the device. Apple’s iOS updates don’t mention it Apple shipped iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3 on Nov. 9, a day after the proof of concept went public. Their security notes list fixes for AirPlay, Bluetooth pairing, brotli and other components, but neither names worse_query or describes a sandbox escape of this kind. That leaves it unclear whether the latest iOS builds block the technique. The exposure depends heavily on how each wallet app stores secrets. item.title: High oil prices have led to a dip in global carbon emissions
item.description: Evaluating the annual global temperatures each year requires context. There is a fair amount of natural variability from one year to the next, so it’s important to focus on the trend over time. Famously, global warming did not end in 1998, as some claimed a couple of decades ago—we just had a run of La-Niña-dominated years after a very strong El Niño. Annual greenhouse gas emissions are much less variable, having increased fairly steadily, but many complicating factors can still muddy the picture. Sometimes those factors conspire to throw a year off the trend. It looks like 2026 will be one of those years. A new analysis led by Corinne Le Quéré at the University of East Anglia estimates that fossil fuel emissions have fallen about 0.4 percent from last year. This probably isn’t a peak that symbolizes heartening progress on climate change, though; the researchers think it’s a short-term dip driven by the war in Iran and its effect on oil prices. item.title: Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes Miami-Dade County Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez said Monday his office has begun accepting bitcoin for property tax payments, both online and in person, while converting every transaction into dollars before the money reaches the county. Fernandez announced the change in a statement on the Tax Collector’s website, calling it a way to give property owners another option without putting public funds into the asset. Payers can select a cryptocurrency option during online checkout or request it at the counter, then connect a supported exchange account or digital wallet and authorize the payment. A third-party system converts the bitcoin into U.S. dollars at the time of payment, the office said, so it never holds, invests in or manages any cryptocurrency. The office said it still receives the full dollar amount owed and records the transactions in its standard payment reports, without county workers maintaining digital wallets. “Government must keep up with the times and the needs of the people we serve,” Fernandez said. “By accepting Bitcoin as a payment option, we are giving property owners another way to pay their taxes, whether online or in person, while continuing to offer the traditional payment methods they already know and trust.” He added that the office is “embracing new technology without compromising our responsibility to protect taxpayer dollars.” Whether someone pays with bitcoin or a conventional method, he said, “our office receives the full amount owed in U.S. dollars.” The office did not name the payment processor or say whether bitcoin payments carry a convenience fee. Card and mobile-wallet payments already carry a nonrefundable 2.50% fee online, with a $2.50 minimum, the office’s payment-methods page shows. Traditional options, including checks, cards, cash and fee-free eChecks, remain available. The announcement covers property taxes, and the option is voluntary. JUST IN: Miami-Dade now accepts Bitcoin for property taxes and can be paid both online and in person pic.twitter.com/lI285z4B79 — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 10, 2026 A 4% discount is still on the clock The change landed in the middle of Florida’s property tax collection season. Miami-Dade opened the 2026 tax roll on Oct. 30 and is urging owners to pay by Nov. 30 to lock in a 4% early-payment discount under Florida law . The discount falls to 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with the full amount due in March. Unpaid bills generally become delinquent April 1. Under the office’s existing rules, discounts are based on the date a payment is submitted online or in person. Fernandez has been promoting a “Save the Max” campaign around that calendar, noting that an eligible $5,000 tax bill would save $200 if paid in November. Payments can be made at the office’s 13 locations, through T-Connect mobile units or online around the clock at mdctaxcollector.gov . Miami’s long c

item.title: Trump taps Palantir security chief to run battered US cyber defense agency
item.description: President Donald Trump has nominated Palantir security chief Michael LoSapio to lead CISA, putting an executive from the controversial government supplier in line to run America's civilian cyber defense agency. The nomination , announced on Monday, could end CISA's nearly two-year wait for a Senate-confirmed director following Jen Easterly's departure in January 2025. LoSapio has served as Palantir's CISO since September 2024 , having previously led the company's infrastructure and network security team. He first joined the data analytics outfit in 2013, later spent a spell at database company SingleStore, and returned to Palantir in 2017. If confirmed, LoSapio would move from securing Palantir's systems to leading the federal government's main civilian cyber defense agency. CISA protects federal civilian networks and works with critical infrastructure operators, including power, water, and telecommunications providers. It's a substantial job, particularly given the state of the agency he would inherit. CISA has shed more than 1,000 staff, roughly a third of its workforce, since Trump returned to the White House, according to reports . It's now trying to plug the gaps, although acting director Nick Andersen said in September that around 250 would-be recruits were still waiting for security clearance before they could get to work. Andersen has been running CISA since February. With fewer people to go around, CISA is also rethinking where to spend its time. A strategy published last month emphasizes infrastructure whose failure would do the most damage, raising questions about what gets less attention as the agency operates with fewer staff. LoSapio would be the second person Trump has put forward for the role. His previous pick, Sean Plankey, withdrew in April after spending more than a year awaiting confirmation, with his nomination becoming caught up in a dispute involving Republican Senator Rick Scott over Coast Guard contracting. The nomination arrives late in the congressional calendar. If the Senate does not confirm LoSapio before the current Congress ends, Trump would have to nominate him again for consideration by the incoming Democratic-controlled Senate. Palantir, co-founded by billionaire Peter Thiel, has become a major supplier of technology to US government agencies, including the Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Its work with immigration authorities has attracted criticism from civil liberties groups and Democratic lawmakers concerned about surveillance and the handling of sensitive personal information. The controversy isn't confined to the US either. In the UK, WhatsApp messages obtained by campaign group Foxglove this week indicate that Palantir privately lobbied a health minister to consider extending its software into GP patient records, despite that data being expressly excluded from its £330 million NHS England contract for the Federated Data Platform.
